question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, the government has allocated Rs. 20000 crores for an initiative aiming to develop at least ______ indigenously designed and operational SMRs by 2033.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• The Union Budget 2025-26 allocated **Rs. 20,000 crores** for an initiative to develop **indigenously designed and operational Small Modular Reactors (SMRs)** by **2033**. 
 
• The goal is to develop at least **5 operational SMRs**, which is considered a feasible and ambitious target for the given timeline and budget allocation. 
 
• **SMRs (Small Modular Reactors)** are advanced nuclear reactors that offer high flexibility, enhanced safety, and lower capital investment compared to traditional nuclear reactors. 
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s goal to enhance **energy security** and reduce **carbon emissions** by adopting cleaner and sustainable energy solutions. 
 
• The development of SMRs will contribute to India’s **Make in India** initiative, promoting indigenous technologies and creating opportunities for skilled employment. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs):** 
 
 
• **Definition:** SMRs are nuclear reactors that are smaller in size, typically producing **up to 300 MW** of electricity per reactor module. 
 
• **Features:** They are designed to be scalable, allowing multiple modules to be combined to meet energy demands. 
 
• **Advantages:** SMRs offer **enhanced safety** features, reduced costs, and shorter construction times compared to conventional nuclear reactors. 
 
• **Applications:** SMRs are ideal for **remote locations, industrial applications, and water desalination**. 
 
 
 
• **Global SMR Development:** 
 
 
• Countries such as **Canada, the US, Russia, and China** are actively investing in SMR technologies. 
 
• Canada’s **National SMR Action Plan** aims to deploy SMRs for clean energy and economic development. 
 
• The US Department of Energy (DOE) has provided funding for SMR development under the **Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program**. 
 
 
 
• **India’s Nuclear Energy Program:** 
 
 
• India currently operates several nuclear power plants and aims to increase its nuclear energy capacity to **22 GW** by 2031. 
 
• Organizations like the **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)** and **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL)** are key players in nuclear energy development. 
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:** 
 
 
• The SMR initiative aligns with the **Make in India** strategy, focusing on indigenous development of advanced technologies. 
 
• This will boost local industries, create jobs, and reduce dependency on foreign technology. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Budget Allocation:** The allocation of **Rs. 20,000 crores** reflects the Indian government’s commitment to advancing nuclear energy technologies. 
 
• **Energy Security:** SMRs will enhance India’s energy security by providing sustainable and reliable power for industrial and residential needs. 
 
• **Carbon Emission Reduction:** Nuclear energy is a clean energy source, and SMRs will play a significant role in reducing India’s dependence on fossil fuels and achieving **climate goals**. 
 
• **Global Collaboration:** India may collaborate with countries already leading in SMR development to gain technical expertise and accelerate deployment.
